To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DLA population is a mix of galaxies with different star formation histories and that the DLA gas reservoir is a significant fraction of the cosmic baryons.

(i) the cosmic neutral gas mass density at z > 2 is a significant fraction of the cosmic baryon density and is comparable to that of stars and (ii) the neutral gas reservoir in the outskirts of high-redshift galaxies is dominated by diffuse gas with star formation efficiencies below the local star formation efficiency.

(1) the DLA gas mass density is consistent with the baryonic mass density inferred from CMB anisotropies and the cosmic star formation history; (2) DLA metallicities increase with redshift; (3) DLA metallicites increase with impact parameter; (4) DLA metallicies increase with gas column density; (5) DLA metallicties decrease with stellar mass; (6) DLA metalliceties are consistent with the chemical enrichment history of galaxies
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physical and chemical properties of the interstellar medium of distant galaxies and the evolution of the cosmic baryonic reservoir.
the following questions: (a) How does the gas in galaxies evolve over the history of the Universe?
the study of the interstellar medium of high-redshift galaxies and the evolution of the intergalactic medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current observational evidence from QSO absorption studies of the neutral and ionized gas in galaxy outskirts is consistent with the predictions of the ΛCDM cosmological model, and that the current observational constraints are not inconsistent with the predictions of semi-analytic models of galaxy formation.

the current observational constraints on the star-formation relation, metallicity evolution, and the ionization structure of gas in the outskirts of galaxies are not sufficient to provide a complete and consistent picture of baryon cycling.
the current empirical understanding of the neutral gas reservoir in the outskirts of galaxies is still very incomplete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DLA data provide a robust picture of the cosmic evolution of the neutral gas content in galaxy outskirts.
the DLA studies provide the most direct and robust evidence of the cosmic neutral reservoir and its evolution.
we have learned that galaxies have a rich circumgalactic environment, and that the gas around them is a key ingredient in the baryon cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutral gas reservoir in the outskirts of galaxies is dominated by diffuse gas, with a mass fraction of ~10% of the baryonic mass of galaxies.
the star formation relation in the outer regions of galaxies is not universal, but depends on galaxy properties.
the cosmic neutral gas in the outskirts of galaxies is the main reservoir of metals in the Universe and is the dominant contributor to the cosmic metal budget.
